intent: Protect buyers from post-agreement AI-agent service substitution by keeping the original accepted manifest immutable, deterministically flagging critical changes, and using GenLayer consensus only for prose-level material equivalence.

frontend.visual_system: web3 protocol console: dark chain-navigation shell, bright transaction surfaces, teal/cyan on-chain accents, agreement-to-substitute gate visualization
frontend.create_form: blank by default; no demo manifest or agreement reference prefilled

security_properties: critical structured changes are deterministic material/no-model
semantic comparison always uses original baseline, not active/intermediate service
material substitution freezes handoff until buyer action
unreported changed declared manifest cannot finalize
provider cannot replace pending material proposal
bounded semantic consensus budget with buyer-only grants
provider withdrawal can only retreat to the already-authorized active manifest
withdrawn candidate remains blocked and cannot reroll
honest_scope: party-declared manifests are not publisher provenance
contract does not verify external-world delivery truth
distinct addresses are contract-local roles, not proof of independent real-world control
equivalent prose substitutions auto-activate by design and have no buyer-side reversal once active
semantic-call bound applies to committed consensus rounds
service_name is intentionally semantic rather than a deterministic critical field
packaging_notes: Production contract source is unchanged by this UI refresh.
Create Agreement is intentionally blank by default; reference case loading remains available elsewhere.
On-chain evidence records executed StudioNet behavior, not source-marker assertions.
Run one fresh Vercel build/smoke after GitHub update before release freeze.
